text: In the past 12 months, has your practice completed a written review of where patient information is stored, who can access it, and what could go wrong?
opts: Yes — completed and documented within the past 12 months
Yes — but it is older than 12 months
Started but never finished, or only informal notes
No formal review has been done

text: When staff log into your EHR, email, or remote access tools, do they need a second step beyond their password — like a text code, app prompt, or fingerprint?
opts: Yes — required on every system that touches patient data
Required on most systems, with a few exceptions
Required on email only, or only some staff
Not required anywhere

text: Are your office laptops, desktops, and portable drives encrypted, so that if one is lost or stolen the patient data on it cannot be read?
opts: Yes — every device is encrypted and verified
Most devices are encrypted; some older ones are not
Only some devices, or unsure how to verify
No encryption is in place

text: Does your practice have automated backups of patient records, and have you successfully tested restoring from a backup in the past 12 months?
opts: Yes — automated backups, and a successful restore test in the past 12 months
Backups exist but a restore has not been tested
Manual or partial backups only
No backups, or unsure

text: If your practice was hit with ransomware or a breach tomorrow, do you have a written plan that names who to call, in what order, and within what timeframe?
opts: Yes — written plan with named roles and tested procedures
Plan exists but has never been tested
Informal procedures only
No plan in place

text: Do you have signed Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) on file with every vendor that touches patient data — EHR, billing service, IT MSP, cloud backup, clearinghouse, transcription, and so on?
opts: Yes — complete vendor list with current BAAs on file
BAAs in place for most vendors; some gaps
BAAs only with the major vendors
No formal BAA inventory or process

text: Has every staff member who handles patient information completed HIPAA security training in the past 12 months, with records on file?
opts: Yes — every staff member, with completion records
Most staff trained, with partial records
Training happens occasionally, no consistent records
No formal HIPAA security training

text: Do you have a documented process for what staff should do — and who they should notify — within 1 hour of losing a phone, laptop, or USB drive that may have contained patient information?
opts: Yes — documented and staff have been trained on it
Process exists but staff are not familiar with it
Informal expectation only
No process

text: Is staff email protected against phishing and business email compromise, with mailbox-level multi-factor authentication and external sender warnings?
opts: Yes — MFA, anti-phishing, and external sender warnings all in place
MFA in place; anti-phishing protections partial
Basic email security only
Standard email with no extra protections

text: When a staff member leaves the practice, is there a written checklist that ensures their EHR, email, and remote access are revoked the same day?
opts: Yes — same-day checklist and verified for every departure
Checklist exists but not always completed
Informal — IT or office manager handles it ad hoc
No process

text: Do your EHR, email, and remote access systems record who accessed what, and does someone at the practice review those logs monthly for unusual activity?
opts: Yes — logs exist and are reviewed monthly
Logs exist but are reviewed rarely or only after incidents
Logs exist but no one reviews them
Logging is minimal or unknown

text: Do you maintain a current list of every technology vendor your practice uses, what patient data they have access to, and when each BAA expires?
opts: Yes — current inventory with data scope and BAA expirations tracked
Inventory exists but is not consistently updated
Partial — major vendors only
No inventory

text: Is there a written policy staff must follow when accessing patient information from a personal phone or laptop, including encryption, screen lock, and remote wipe?
opts: Yes — written policy with technical controls enforced
Policy exists but enforcement is inconsistent
Informal expectation only
Personal devices are used freely with no policy

text: If patient information was compromised, does your practice know the timelines and required steps under HIPAA, HITECH, and your state breach notification law?
opts: Yes — documented in our incident response plan with named roles
Generally aware but not documented
Aware of HIPAA only, not HITECH or state law
Not familiar with the requirements
